claims.claim: p4c_build fits the carries `other` mass on a TEAM-carries denominator: pool = clip(mall - ms, 0, 0.95) with mall summing every position.

Over the 2,718 pre-2026 team-games excluding 2020, mall has mean 1.00000000, min 0.9999999999999998, max 1.0000000000000002 and ZERO team-games deviating by more than 1e-6. The fitted quantity is therefore exactly 1 - (modelled RBs share of TEAM carries).

claims.claim: WS02: "the registered 0.1918 is the 2020-INCLUSIVE figure, so the two terms in the identification argument are drawn from different populations", and the same population mismatch propagated into 0.008754 / 22.7x.
claims.stated_in: WS02_C1_VERIFICATION.md items 5 and 6 and its Bottom Line
claims.basis: The population is not the driver, and it pulls the wrong way. Running OWN-5's own estimator on panel_p3: ALL seasons -> non-RB 0.191779 (this IS the registered 0.1918); EXCLUDING 2020 -> 0.191861, which moves AWAY from 0.1902 by +0.000082. Running the FIT's estimator on the SAME 2020-inclusive population -> 0.190015, not 0.1918. Decomposition through denominator.py:193's own formula: holding the estimator fixed and changing the population moves `correct_other` by -0.000101 (OWN-5 estimator) or -0.000193 (fit estimator); holding the population fixed and changing the estimator moves it by +0.002159 (all seasons) or +0.002066 (ex-2020). The estimator is worth ten to twenty times the population and it is the only term with the right sign. The real cause: own5/audit_rush_ownership.historical_from_panel uses a DIFFERENT ESTIMATOR on a DIFFERENT SOURCE FILE with a DIFFERENT DENOMINATOR COLUMN -- ratio-of-means of raw `carries` over `team_rush_att`, read from nfl/research/inputs/panel_p3.csv.gz -- against the fit's mean of per-team-game summed `s_carries` over `team_carries`, read from p4b/panel_enriched.pkl. The two denominator columns have the same mean (26.9157 on the ex-2020 window), so this is a Jensen gap between ratio-of-means and mean-of-ratios, not a data-window gap.
claims.note: WS02's CORRECTED VALUES (0.010774, 18.46x, "they differ by 0.0071") all stand; only its causal explanation is withdrawn. This matters operationally: the remedy WS02's diagnosis implies -- align the season windows -- would move the number by 0.0002 and leave the discrepancy entirely intact.

claims.claim: The bootstrap clusters on team-game and reports its cluster count beside every interval.
claims.basis: row_cluster = f"{team}_{ord}" with ord = season*100 + week, so no 2022 team-game can merge with a 2023 one. Per-season 542 + 544 + 544 = 1,630 = the pooled n_clusters, matching the frame the WS-H brief declares. block_boot resamples clusters with replacement and forms the ratio of sums, which is correct for unequal cluster sizes, and returns None below 5 clusters rather than a thin interval. Arms are paired on the same W, the same appearance draws and the same rng index array.

claims.claim: WS02: "observed ratio 1.2248 against the algebraic prediction (1 - 0.010774)/(1 - 0.198875) = 1.2347; the gap is degenerate groups and per-draw pool resampling."
claims.registered_value: the gap is degenerate groups and per-draw pool resampling
claims.re_derived_value: the gap is the per-draw pool resample alone; degenerate groups cannot contribute to it
claims.basis: A degenerate group has S = 0 for every row in BOTH arms, so it contributes zero to both means and cancels out of the ratio exactly. It cannot explain any part of the gap. The resample alone explains all of it: drawing w_other with a matched index array of shape (2, 200) from the two fitted pools 2,000 times gives a ratio of 1.234925 +/- 0.008517, 95% [1.219030, 1.252441], which contains the observed 1.224798. Both the observed ratio (1.224798) and the algebraic prediction (1.234797) reproduce WS02 to four decimals on a DIFFERENT budget, which is itself the direct proof that the ratio is budget-scale invariant.

There is a FOURTH, and it is the one closest to the code: p4c_lib.allocate's own docstring at p4c_lib.py:101 still states the superseded formula "simplex: S_i = w_i A_i / (sum_g w A + w_other)", four lines above the comment explaining that that formula was replaced. WS02 missed it.

claims.claim: A hardcoded 0.0088 sits in the committed test, and the test passes anyway.

Demonstrated rather than argued: substituting the REAL fitted pools (0.198875 / 0.010774) into the module and re-running test_a leaves all three checks passing, the only visible change being the printed detail "22.6x" becoming "18.5x". The three checks are (1) an assertion about an array the function just built, (2) abs(0.1989 - 0.1918) < 0.01, which compares two literals and reads no code at all, and (3) a ratio > 10 threshold that 18.46 and 22.7 both clear. So test_a pins a partition value the code does not produce and is structurally unable to notice. run_suite.py --only test_c1_denominator at HEAD: modules 1, test functions 7, checks 25, FAILING CHECKS 0, RAISED 0, SUITE PASS -- and that green says nothing about either number it was written to guard.

corrected_evaluation.coverage_note: On the corrected oracle both arms OVER-cover: C1 reaches 0.6992 / 0.8985 / 0.9549 against nominal 0.50 / 0.80 / 0.90, and BASELINE 0.6141 / 0.8078 / 0.8899. The shipped artifact's apparently near-nominal coverage was a product of the short budget. Interpretation is constrained: 40.6-44.9% of scored rows have a realised zero and the predictive distribution carries a large point mass at zero, so interval coverage is lumpy and a percentile interval is conservative by construction. This is recorded, not diagnosed, and no adequacy claim is made.

suite.caveat: A green here is not behavioural proof of the two registered numbers. test_a fabricates its inputs; substituting the real fitted pools leaves all three of its checks passing.

honest_statement_of_the_result: C1 corrects a real denominator mismatch. It raises the modelled running backs share of the budget they are dealt by a factor of 1.230 (1.222 to 1.235 by season, invariant to the budget level to six decimals), and on a correctly-scaled oracled budget it improves pooled carry CRPS by 0.182997, with a team-game clustered 95% interval of [-0.195603, -0.170441] over 1,630 clusters, in the same direction in all three evaluation seasons with every per-season interval excluding zero. The applied `other` mass is 0.010774 against a fitted 0.198875, an 18.46x overstatement. Receiving is bit-identical and the frozen Q9 candidate identity is unchanged. The result is EXPLORATORY: the defect was found by inspecting the data the evaluation then scored. No equivalence margin and no TOST were predeclared, so nothing here supports a claim that any quantity is unbiased, stable, closed or correct.
known_ceilings: Chronology is not provable from this repository: pre-registration, estimator, harness, result and test are one commit.

The "unmodelled running back" population is a proxy (f_n_prior >= 1 is not the production depth-chart pool), as the pre-registration itself declares. The comparison is unaffected; the LEVEL 0.010774 is only as good as the proxy.
The corrected budget is still ORACLED. It isolates the allocation layer, which is the layer under test, and its numbers are not comparable with run_p4c or with any live forecast.
A1's rb share is fit on seasons that include all three evaluation seasons. Held identical across arms; still unstated in any committed artifact.
The bootstrap resamples team-games only. Monte Carlo error from the 400 draws, the appearance draws and the single W realisation sits inside the point estimate, not inside the interval.
Only test_c1_denominator was run. Whether the repair disturbs any other suite is out of scope here.
